analysis_notes.note: Torah #117 discusses a specific spiritual phenomenon: when a person enters high kedusha (e.g., draws close to the true tzaddik), the yetzer hara intensifies and an impure occurrence (mikre bilti tahor) may happen. The Rebbe explains this through a causal chain: entering kedusha -> strictened din from above -> the dinim chain down (hishtalshelus hadinim) -> the yetzer hara is generated -> the impure occurrence. He also explains that hidden tuma (tuma temuna) is expelled when one approaches kedusha, which is actually beneficial because it can then be rectified. Biblical examples: Avraham begat Yishmael before Yitzchak, Yitzchak begat Esav before Yaakov — to expel the zuhama first. All relationships in this torah are causal/eitza-type: kedusha causes dinim, dinim cause yetzer hara, approaching holiness causes hidden tuma to emerge. The reference to the Kohen Gadol on Yom Kippur not having a mikre being counted as a miracle reinforces the causal framework. No bechina (parallel-aspect / shared-nature) statements of the form 'X hu bechinat Y' appear anywhere in the text.
